propositions: Merge-abort recovery logic is duplicated across sync.py and push_recovery.py, with the two implementations having already diverged in behavior (push_recovery checks git status for ?? paths before moving; sync does not).

push_recovery.py reaches into sync.py for shared pieces (_quarantine_dir_under, _untracked_overwrite_paths) to work around an architectural constraint: all git calls must route through late-bound core._git seam rather than sync's module-level _git to support monkeypatching.
The same defect has landed independently in both code paths twice (bugs small-delicious-loris and sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey), illustrating the instalment pattern that consolidation prevents.
A third caller, _commands/doctor.py::_quarantine_leftovers, uses sync._quarantine_untracked directly, creating blast radius for any changes to the duplicated logic.

Consolidation must preserve existing adapter signatures and symbols (sync and push_recovery keep delegating stubs) so that existing monkeypatch sites and direct test calls continue to work without modification.

The new merge_recovery.py module accepts git as a callable parameter, allowing both sync's module-level _git and push_recovery's late-bound core._git to be supplied, unifying the two implementations while respecting their different patch points.
